commit_order: This protocol is committed before the new adaptive learner, evaluation harness, or focused tests.
question: Can surprise-sensitive, evidence-grounded retrieval react earlier than a 12-observation fixed gate and still learn a new reversed rule without phase labels?
simulator: Unchanged ObservableWorld two-number route / route-reversed simulator; engineered features and rules explicitly NOT evidence of unfamiliar-family generalization.

evaluation.random_baseline: Independent seeded random TEST action policy, not used to gather training outcomes; shares test tasks with all methods.

source_actor: Independent deterministic random first-action observer, one action per training episode; every harmful action counted once regardless of number of checkpoints or baseline methods. Test policies never choose data-acquisition actions.

fast_retrieval.candidates: All chronologically complete 64-observation nonoverlapping archive blocks that END BEFORE the last 4 scoring events, plus a recent 8-observation candidate from the 8 events immediately prior to those scoring events
fast_retrieval.scoring: Mean log likelihood over the last four observed feedback events with 0.05 Laplace smoothing; no hidden regime or phase labels; k=5 numeric nearest-neighbor outcome estimator.
fast_retrieval.tie_break: Choose archived candidate before recent candidate; among archives choose earliest index.
fast_retrieval.checkpoints: Replay full ordered observed event log, SHA256 integrity, reconstructed decisions after restart.
fast_retrieval.evidence_limitations: Recent candidate can be noisy or misleading, and last-four evidence can be too small to detect a change. Selection thresholds are hand-designed and no uncertainty guarantee is claimed.

frozen_acceptance: Fast retrieval should improve return-A at <=8 new observations over fixed-12 and cumulative baselines, and improve B at 12 or 24 over fixed-12, without losing more than 5 percentage points at B160. All improvements measured with identical seeds, training data, and evaluation tasks. Preserve failures even if thresholds fail.
boundaries: Repeated test tasks across checkpoints are not independent samples
